subject.title: Discord ingress stalls behind main event loop — mirror the Telegram isolated-worker fix (#81132)

question: Should Discord adopt a plugin-owned worker and SQLite-backed ingress queue, or should OpenClaw first solve the shared event-loop starvation and backpressure path without adding a second channel-specific isolation architecture?
rationale: Discord’s persistent gateway session has heartbeat, resume, sequence, and reconnect invariants that differ materially from Telegram polling, and the available production evidence does not yet establish which ownership boundary provides the safest durable fix.

options.title: Sponsor isolated Discord ingress
options.body: Keep the WebSocket and heartbeat loop in a Discord-owned worker, bridge normalized events through SQLite-backed plugin state, and require saturation plus reconnect/resume proof.

options.title: Fix shared starvation first
options.body: Profile the heavy tool-output and sidecar paths, add yielding or backpressure at the shared source, and reconsider channel isolation only if Discord remains vulnerable.

options.title: Accept the current coupling
options.body: Retain the main-thread gateway architecture and document operational load limits, accepting intermittent latency and reconnect risk during severe stalls.

recommendation.title: Sponsor isolated Discord ingress
recommendation.body: Keep the WebSocket and heartbeat loop in a Discord-owned worker, bridge normalized events through SQLite-backed plugin state, and require saturation plus reconnect/resume proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The Telegram worker/spool implementation provides the closest merged architectural precedent and its author is best positioned to assess which invariants carry over to Discord.
